questions.q: Six friends M, N, O, P, Q, and R are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. M sits second to the left of N. O sits exactly opposite to M. P sits to the immediate right of N. Q is not adjacent to M. Who sits to the immediate left of O?
questions.s:
Let N = Pos 1. 
M is 2nd left of N (Clockwise direction) -> M = Pos 3.
O is opposite M -> O = Pos 6.
P is immediate right of N (Anti-clockwise) -> P = Pos 2.
Q is not adjacent to M (Pos 3). Empty slots are 4 and 5. Adjacent to M are 2 and 4. Thus Q cannot be at 4. Q = Pos 5.
R takes the remaining Pos 4.
Order (Clockwise starting from N=1): N(1), P(2), M(3), R(4), Q(5), O(6).
Immediate left of O(6) is N(1).

questions.q: A and B start a business. A invests ₹80,000 for 9 months, B invests ₹1,20,000 for 6 months. What is B's share of a ₹45,000 profit?
questions.s:
Given:

A invests ₹80,000 for 9 months

B invests ₹1,20,000 for 6 months

Total Profit = ₹45,000

Formula used:

Profit ratio = Capital × Time

Calculations:

⇒ A’s investment = 80,000 × 9 = 7,20,000

⇒ B’s investment = 1,20,000 × 6 = 7,20,000

⇒ Ratio = 7,20,000 : 7,20,000

⇒ Ratio = 1 : 1

⇒ Total ratio = 2

⇒ B’s share = 1 / 2 × 45,000

⇒ B’s share = 22,500

∴ B’s share of the profit is ₹22,500.

questions.q: In a hotel, ration is available for 148 persons for 51 days. If 37 persons left the hotel, then for how many days will the remaining ration last?
questions.s:
Given:

In a hotel, ration is available for 148 persons for 51 days. If 37 persons left the hotel.

Calculations:

If 148 persons consume ration for 51 days

Then, 1 person can consume ration for 51 × 148 days

Now 37 person left then only (148 - 37) = 111 persons are available

So, 111 persons can consume ration for

$\frac{148 × 51}{111}$

= 68

Hence, The Required number of days is 68 days.

Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

What renders the draft legislation particularly contentious is not its proposed realignment of fiscal powers per se, (1)/ but that it presumes, without empirical substantiation, (2)/ a fiscal equivalence among states whose developmental baselines are (3)/ incommensurable by any normative metric. (4)
questions.s:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • The error is located in part (2) of the sentence due to a lack of parallel structure (parallelism).
  • The sentence uses the correlative construction "is not [A] but [B]." For grammatical precision, both [A] and [B] should belong to the same grammatical category.
  • In part (1), [A] is a noun phrase ("its proposed realignment..."). In part (2), [B] is a noun clause ("that it presumes...").
  • To correct this, [B] should be changed to a noun phrase to match [A], such as "its presumption... of a fiscal equivalence."
  • Thus, the error is found in part (2).
Therefore, the correct answer is 2.
 
Correct Sentence: "What renders the draft legislation particularly contentious is not its proposed realignment of fiscal powers per se, but its presumption, without empirical substantiation, of a fiscal equivalence among states whose developmental baselines are incommensurable by any normative metric."
 
Additional Information
  • (1): "What renders the draft legislation particularly contentious is not its proposed realignment..." – This part correctly uses a free relative clause ("What renders...") as the subject and establishes the first half of the contrast.
  • (3): "a fiscal equivalence among states whose developmental baselines are" – This is grammatically correct; "among" is appropriate for a group of states, and the plural verb "are" agrees with "baselines."
  • (4): "incommensurable by any normative metric." – This part is correct. "Incommensurable" means lacking a basis of comparison, and "by" is the correct preposition when referring to the standard or metric of measurement.

Which event occurs around June 21st, when the Northern Hemisphere is tilted most directly toward the Sun, resulting in the longest day of the year? / कौन सी घटना 21 जून के आसपास होती है, जब उत्तरी गोलार्ध सूर्य की ओर सबसे सीधे झुका होता है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप वर्ष का सबसे लंबा दिन होता है?
questions_hin.s_hi: On this day, the Sun is directly overhead at the Tropic of Cancer.

questions_hin.q_hi: एक व्यक्ति अपनी आय का 16 2/3% बचाता है। यदि बचत में 36% की वृद्धि होती है और व्यय में 60% की वृद्धि होती है, तो उसकी आय में प्रतिशत वृद्धि है:
The phenomenon where the Moon appears reddish during a total lunar eclipse is often called what? / पूर्ण चंद्र ग्रहण के दौरान चंद्रमा के लाल दिखाई देने की घटना को अक्सर क्या कहा जाता है?
questions_hin.s_hi: This occurs because sunlight is refracted through Earth's atmosphere, scattering blue light and allowing red light to reach the Moon.

questions_hin.q_hi: The ratio between the expenditure and saving of Shyam is $4:5$. When Shyam increases his expenditure by $12\%$ and increases his saving by $5\%$, what would have been the percentage increase in his income?
questions_hin.s_hi: Dekh bhai, zeros laga de calculation easy karne ke liye. Exp = 400, Sav = 500, Inc = 900. Exp bada $12\%$ yani $48$. Sav bada $5\%$ yani $25$. Nayi Income me net increment = $48 + 25 = 73$. Base income $900$ thi, toh percentage = $\frac{73}{900} \times 100 = 8.11\%$. CGL me data hamesha zero laga ke halwa ho jata hai.

questions_hin.q_hi: A और B की आय का अनुपात 5:4 है, जबकि उनके व्यय का अनुपात क्रमशः 6:7 है। यदि A और B क्रमशः 4,000 और 1,000 रुपये बचाते हैं, तो उनके व्यय के बीच का अंतर कितना है?

Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

What renders the draft legislation particularly contentious is not its proposed realignment of fiscal powers per se, (1)/ but that it presumes, without empirical substantiation, (2)/ a fiscal equivalence among states whose developmental baselines are (3)/ incommensurable by any normative metric. (4)
questions_hin.s_hi:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • The error is located in part (2) of the sentence due to a lack of parallel structure (parallelism).
  • The sentence uses the correlative construction "is not [A] but [B]." For grammatical precision, both [A] and [B] should belong to the same grammatical category.
  • In part (1), [A] is a noun phrase ("its proposed realignment..."). In part (2), [B] is a noun clause ("that it presumes...").
  • To correct this, [B] should be changed to a noun phrase to match [A], such as "its presumption... of a fiscal equivalence."
  • Thus, the error is found in part (2).
Therefore, the correct answer is 2.
 
Correct Sentence: "What renders the draft legislation particularly contentious is not its proposed realignment of fiscal powers per se, but its presumption, without empirical substantiation, of a fiscal equivalence among states whose developmental baselines are incommensurable by any normative metric."
 
Additional Information
  • (1): "What renders the draft legislation particularly contentious is not its proposed realignment..." – This part correctly uses a free relative clause ("What renders...") as the subject and establishes the first half of the contrast.
  • (3): "a fiscal equivalence among states whose developmental baselines are" – This is grammatically correct; "among" is appropriate for a group of states, and the plural verb "are" agrees with "baselines."
  • (4): "incommensurable by any normative metric." – This part is correct. "Incommensurable" means lacking a basis of comparison, and "by" is the correct preposition when referring to the standard or metric of measurement.
